images.title: 5 kg 200 g minus 2 kg 800 g in a column
images.purpose: Show how to subtract weights when the g on top are fewer: break 1 kg into 1,000 g, so 5 kg 200 g becomes 4 kg 1,200 g and the answer is 2 kg 400 g.
images.composition: A two column subtraction with the top weight broken, the result below the line, and three note boxes at the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. COLUMN HEADS at y 130: the unit kg (44 px, bold, teal #0072B2) centred at x 420 and the unit g (44 px, bold, amber-dark #E69F00) centred at x 720. ROW 1 at y 280: the top weight after the break: the digit 5 centred at x 420 crossed by a thin diagonal line (3 px, #6B7280) with the digit 4 above it at y 235 (circled, 44 px circle with a 3 px outline #CC79A7), and the digits 200 centred at x 720 crossed by a thin diagonal line with 1,200 above it at y 235 (circled, 100 by 48 px oval with a 3 px outline #CC79A7); the uncrossed digits 5 and 200 in 64 px, bold, dark #1F2937, the new numbers 4 and 1,200 in 40 px, bold, #CC79A7. ROW 2 at y 380: the sign − (minus, U+2212) at x 280, then 2 centred at x 420 and 800 centred at x 720 (64 px, bold, dark #1F2937). RULE LINE: a dark #1F2937 horizontal line 4 px thick at y 440 from x 220 to x 920. RESULT ROW at y 530: 2 centred at x 420 and 400 centred at x 720 (64 px, bold, teal #0072B2). NOTE BOX at the right, a rounded rectangle 440 by 130 px at x 960 to 1400, y 260 to 390, filled #F3F4F6 with a 3 px outline #6B7280, containing the text Break 1 kg into 1,000 g (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Under it a second box a rounded rectangle 440 by 100 px at x 960 to 1400, y 410 to 510, filled #F3F4F6 with a 3 px outline #6B7280, containing the text 1,200 − 800 = 400 g (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Under it a third box a rounded rectangle 440 by 100 px at x 960 to 1400, y 530 to 630, filled #F3F4F6 with a 3 px outline #6B7280, containing the text 4 − 2 = 2 kg (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: When the g on top are fewer, break 1 kg into 1,000 g first: 5 kg 200 g − 2 kg 800 g = 2 kg 400 g.
images.description: A column subtraction of 2 kg 800 g from 5 kg 200 g with 1 kg broken into 1,000 g, giving 2 kg 400 g.
images.context: Concept image for Subtracting Weights. It follows the idea of the kg and g column with a break in your maths book and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Say why 800 g cannot be taken from 200 g before the break. The slip to watch: taking the smaller number from the bigger in each column.

image_decisions.why: The crossed 5 and the new 4 and 1,200 show the break as a picture.
